registered: 2026-11-25, before KinematiK's convection correlation was evaluated for this disc. DISCLOSURE: the CFD tables were read before this file was written (they had to be, to find the inputs). The friction-ring inner radius is not given in the thesis; it is derived from the thesis's own inner-friction-surface heat and HTC at 30 C (A = Q / (h dT)), and that choice is fixed here before KinematiK is run.

source.reference: Chandrasekar, Numerical Heat Transfer Simulations of Brake Discs under Dyno-Test Load Cases, MSc thesis, Chalmers University of Technology, 2026 (industrial supervisor Volvo Cars Propulsion Components)
source.tool: Simcenter STAR-CCM+ conjugate CFD of the dynamometer enclosure (104 M cells, mesh-converged), checked by the author against thermocouple data in a test rotor via an Abaqus transient model
source.disc: Brake disc 1: ventilated, 366 mm OD, 28 mm thick; dynamic rolling radius 0.3725 m (180 km/h = 1281.78 rpm, thesis Table 5.2); air 20 C; rig inlet 300 m3/h
source.tables: A.1 (HTC by surface and temperature, 180 km/h), A.3 (heat by surface, 180 km/h), A.6 (HTC of VC, IFS, OFS by speed, 500 C, clockwise)

mapping.kinematik: h_rotating_disc(366, v, wheel_radius_mm=372.5, crossflow_ms=0) x convective_area_m2(366, hat_clearance_mm=r_out - r_in, default area_factor 2.4). Cross-flow is set to zero because on the dynamometer the air does not cross the disc at road speed: it comes from a 300 m3/h rig inlet. So this tests the rotating-disc term and the area model, not the car cross-flow term.
mapping.test_1: whole-disc convective conductance at 180 km/h, W/K: CFD sum over the eight surfaces of Q / (T - 20) at 100 to 800 C, against KinematiK h x A_conv
mapping.test_2: speed scaling at 500 C: the area-weighted mean HTC of VC, IFS and OFS (areas from A.1 and A.3 at 500 C) at 30 to 280 km/h, divided by its value at 180 km/h, against KinematiK h(v) / h(180)
